object_description: long extruded structure with a continuous uniform profile
design_condition: The long structure occupies one side of the site to create a generous green area, but its scale and proximity to the surrounding streets reduce permeability, visual connections, and sensitivity to the existing trees.

positive.statement: The cleverly developed sectional figure is fascinating in its representative potential.

position.rationale: Long continuous massing and uniform sectional profile are clearly visible across plan and elevations.

positive.statement: The main access arrangement naturally connects the building to the site and establishes clear spatial order.

position.rationale: Main access is anchored approximately along the south-facing ground edge connecting building and site.

positive.statement: The interconnected indoor and outdoor spaces promise daily added value for school life.

position.rationale: Central plan openings and lower-level edges provide an approximate anchor for connected indoor-outdoor areas.

positive.statement: The entrance hall’s view of the gymnasium contributes to a specific spatial atmosphere.

position.rationale: Interior hall and gymnasium are not distinguishable, so placement follows the likely south entrance zone.

positive.statement: Large contiguous areas with logical development offer scope for future change and a sustainable life cycle.

position.rationale: The elongated building footprint visibly supports broad contiguous areas along its length.

positive.statement: The architectural identity is impressive and the materialization is believable.

position.rationale: Material identity is assigned to the visible exterior envelope, especially the long facade.

negative.statement: The building’s considerable dimension strains the site’s characteristic permeability and visual references.

position.rationale: The unusually elongated footprint is directly evident in plan and longitudinal elevations.

negative.statement: Its extension into the street space affects surrounding trees and does not convincingly address the street.

position.rationale: Street impact is approximated along the south edge where the long building meets surrounding open space.

negative.statement: The uniform height and structure require stronger differentiation to integrate into the district and gain social acceptance.

position.rationale: Repeated horizontal elevation bands and consistent top profile clearly show uniform height and structure.

negative.statement: A single main entrance with long internal corridors may not provide a pleasant arrival for the whole school.

position.target: single main entrance and long internal corridors
position.rationale: Entrance and corridor system is approximated from the elongated plan and south-side access constraint.

negative.statement: The uniform facade makes it difficult for children to identify and orient themselves at their entrances.

position.rationale: Long elevations visibly repeat a uniform facade treatment with limited differentiation.

negative.statement: The roof-level outdoor spaces may not be sufficiently available to the district outside school hours.

position.rationale: Roof areas are approximated on the visible upper envelope without distinguishable terrace boundaries.

negative.statement: The jury missed additional public leisure and play opportunities at ground level.

position.target: ground-level public leisure and play opportunities
position.rationale: Ground-level public space is anchored in the open strip adjacent to the building’s south side.

negative.statement: Running tracks and parking occupy an atmospheric arrival space that should instead provide quality of stay.

position.rationale: Arrival-space uses are approximated along the ground-level edge beside the elongated structure.

negative.statement: The functional areas appear monotonous, and further transversal crossings are needed to improve orientation and district connections.

position.rationale: The long repetitive plan suggests monotonous internal zones requiring additional transverse connections.

negative.statement: The SKB bus route could intersect undesirably with schoolchildren’s movements.

position.target: SKB bus route and schoolchildren movements
position.rationale: Bus interaction is approximated at the south-west ground edge where external circulation meets school access.

negative.statement: Classrooms facing an inward courtyard without an outside view are criticized.

position.rationale: Classroom placement is approximated around the central inward-facing plan region.

negative.statement: There is no clear arrival room for the SKB on the ground floor.

position.rationale: Ground-floor arrival is anchored near the south-facing entrance edge, without a distinguishable room marker.

negative.statement: The revised circulation becomes too narrow around staircases and would cause considerable operational problems.

position.rationale: Stair and circulation constraints are approximated within the repetitive interior plan.

negative.statement: The absence of ground-level play options is a missed opportunity for the neighbourhood.

position.rationale: Missing play provision is anchored to the accessible ground strip adjoining the building.

negative.statement: The large facade area, terraces and footprint weaken economic efficiency, ecology and generally accessible open space.

position.target: large facade area, terraces and footprint
position.rationale: Extensive footprint and facade surfaces are directly visible, while terraces are approximated on the envelope.
